title: Fee-funded compute
oneLiner: An agent whose coin's creator fees pay for GPU time: it claims the fees, rents compute within a budget they cover, runs a workload in public, and posts the books on the coin's page.
solToStart: about 0.1 SOL, plus a funded account with a GPU provider
outside: A GPU rental provider with an API (you pick it, and fund it yourself)
howItWorks: Launches one coin from the agent's own wallet. The coin's story is the compute it pays for.
Places a fee-claim order that collects the creator fees every day.
Keeps a ledger: fees claimed in, compute spent out. It only rents GPU time while the ledger says the fees cover it.
Rents GPUs through a provider's API, runs the project's workload (say, an open model serving or a batch job), and stops the rental when the budget or the job runs out.
Posts the books on the coin's page: fees claimed, GPU hours bought, what they ran. Plain text, a few times a day at most.
earns: The coin's creator fees, from trading in it. Here they're spent, not kept: the point is compute paid for by the coin's trading, with public books. Selling that compute to others is a later milestone, not the start.
costs: Launch: higher.fun's launch fee (0.02 SOL) plus about 0.025 SOL of rent and network fees.
GPU time, at the provider's prices, paid from an account you fund (usually by card or stablecoin). Highwire can't pay the provider for you.
Claims: Solana network fees only; Highwire charges nothing on claims.
needs: An account and API key with a GPU rental provider
A machine that stays on for the order runner and the agent's loop
risks: This is the hardest idea: real infrastructure, a real provider bill, and moving money between the wallet and the provider is your job.
Creator fees may be far smaller than GPU prices. The budget rule keeps spending within what came in, which may be very little.
A rental left running costs money until it's stopped. The agent stops rentals itself, but check the provider's dashboard.
Keep the provider's API key in .env, never in the repository.

milestones.title: M1 · Skeleton and a dry-run launch
milestones.summary: Setup, the coin's details, and a launch that passes the policy and simulates, without sending.

milestones.title: M2 · The ledger and a fake provider
milestones.summary: The provider interface, the budget rule and the books, all tested without spending anything.

milestones.title: M3 · Going live and claiming (you, then the agent)
milestones.summary: Launch for real, then a daily fee-claim order feeding the ledger.

milestones.title: M4 · A real provider
milestones.summary: One adapter for the provider you chose, quote-only until you allow spending.

milestones.title: M5 · The workload and the books
milestones.summary: Rent, run, stop, and post the numbers on the coin's page.

prompt: Read PRD.md and AGENTS.md, then build milestone 1. Keep the policy a dry run: never set "live" yourself, and never spend money with a provider without my go-ahead.

day.text: You deploy the template, run setup, and your coding agent builds milestone 1 and the ledger with a fake provider. Nothing is spent anywhere.
You launch the coin for real, pick a GPU provider, fund its account, and put its API key in .env. Spending stays off until you allow it.
A fee-claim order collects the creator fees. The agent books each claim in its ledger as income.
The agent rents GPU time within what the fees have earned, runs the workload, stops the rental, and books the spend.
It posts the books on the coin's page: fees claimed, GPU hours bought, what they ran.

policyNotes.actions: Launch and claim only: no trading and no transfers, so SOL leaves the wallet only by your hand.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_tx: Room for the launch fee and a small first buy.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_day: A daily cap on anything the wallet spends.
policyNotes.max_slippage_bps: Only matters for the first buy at launch.
policyNotes.orders: Only fee-claim orders, at most two open.
policyNotes.posts: Comments on its own coin only, at most three a day, no site chat.

faq.q: How does SOL become GPU time?
faq.a: Not through Highwire. Providers bill a card or stablecoin account, so you fund the provider; the agent only rents within what the coin's fees have earned, and shows the books.
Any with an API. The PRD keeps every call behind one small interface, so you can pick one and swap it later.

faq.q: Can a rental run away with my money?
faq.a: The agent stops every rental it starts, never rents past its allowance, daily cap or hours per run, and only spends at all once you set allow_spend. Still, check the provider's dashboard.
That's the project's story: an open model serving a community, a nightly batch job, generated art for the coin. The PRD leaves it to you, in src/workload.ts.
It's the hardest idea here. Creator fees may be far smaller than GPU prices; the calculator above shows what a given volume would pay for.
